title: Robotics Corner: NormaCore Lamp, a Printable Robot Desk Lamp
description: Five bus servos, 17 printed parts and about $140 in parts: an open-source lamp that moves like a character

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: NormaCore Lamp
slides.body: NormaCore open-sourced Lamp on October 14: a fully 3D-printed desk lamp with 5 degrees of freedom that swivels, folds, tilts and rolls its shade. A small robot first and a light second.

slides.heading: Printing and Parts
bullets: 17 printed parts in 12 shapes, about 48 hours of printing, plus a PETG window disc in the shade
Five ST3215 12 V bus servos on one serial bus, the same servo family as the SO-101
About $140 for the simple version, about $160 for the LED version (README estimates)
Base ballast is three M16 hex bolts and six nuts, about 585 g of steel
Editable CAD, print files, firmware and simulation assets are all in the repo

slides.heading: Two Ways to Build It
bullets: Simple: servo adapter in the base, driven from your computer over USB
LED: an ESP32-CAM and a WS2812B ring in the head, with its own Wi-Fi web page, REST API and program editor
Same printed arm for both, so you can upgrade the head later without reprinting
Heads-up from the README: the base and head joints have no end stops, so don't force them past 90 degrees by hand

slides.heading: Bonus for SO-101 Owners
slides.body: Foxglove's October 23 post adds record-and-replay to a ROS 2 stack for the SO-101: hand-guide or teleop a motion, save it as an MCAP file, and play it back through collision-checked teleop. Still a work in progress.
